# datadog_derived_metric (Resource)

Provides a Datadog derived metric resource. A derived metric is computed from a formula over one or more metric queries. Managing derived metrics requires the `Manage Tags for Metrics` permission.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Create a derived metric that combines two metric queries
resource "datadog_derived_metric" "cpu_total" {
  name    = "custom.cpu.total"
  formula = "a + b"
  queries = [
    {
      name        = "a"
      data_source = "metrics"
      query       = "avg:system.cpu.user{*}"
    },
    {
      name        = "b"
      data_source = "metrics"
      query       = "avg:system.cpu.system{*}"
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `formula` (String) The formula that combines the queries into the value of the derived metric. Queries are referenced by their `name`.
- `name` (String) The name of the derived metric. This field can't be updated after creation.
- `queries` (Attributes List) The list of queries referenced by the formula. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--queries))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

<a id="nestedatt--queries"></a>
### Nested Schema for `queries`

Required:

- `data_source` (String) The data source that the query is run against, for example `metrics`.
- `name` (String) The name used to reference this query from the formula.
- `query` (String) The query string executed against the data source.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Derived metrics can be imported using their name, e.g.
terraform import datadog_derived_metric.cpu_total "custom.cpu.total"
```
